articles.title: Incoming Mississauga mayor pushes for provincial funding during first Queen's Park visit
articles.summary: During his first visit to Queen's Park since being elected mayor of Mississauga, Alvin Tedjo says he's pushing for more financial support from the province to help him address some key priorities.

articles.title: Ex-secretary of Serbian Orthodox Diocese of Canada charged with fraud over missing $200K: Halton police
articles.summary: The ex-secretary of the Serbian Orthodox Diocese of Canada, located in Milton, Ont., has been arrested and charged with fraud after a police investigation found over $200,000 went missing from the diocese.

articles.title: At least one person dead, QEW fully closed in Niagara Falls crash involving tractor trailer
articles.summary: At least one person has died and the Queen Elizabeth Way (QEW) is closed in both directions following a three-vehicle crash in Niagara Falls. Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) say the crash, which involved a tractor trailer, happened between Thorold Stone Road and Mountain Road Wednesday afternoon. articles.title: TTC adjusting service on Queen St. E. for streetcar track renewal, sewer rehabilitation work
articles.summary: The TTC says it is adjusting service along Queen St. E. to accommodate the renewal of aging streetcar tracks and sewer rehabilitation work. Preliminary rail welding work is already underway between Leslie and Laing streets, with 501/301 Queen streetcars diverting via Gerrard Street East between Broadview and Coxwell avenues. articles.title: Early childhood educators call out Ontario over wage freeze, while child care capped at $22 until 2027
articles.summary: Early childhood educators called out the Ford government at Queen's Park Wednesday after a recent memo revealed a wage floor freeze and that workers will not receive an expected annual $1-per-hour increase in 2027.

articles.title: Man dead following industrial incident in Scarborough: police
articles.summary: A man is dead after an industrial incident that happened just before noon Wednesday near McNicoll Avenue and Tapscott Road, Toronto police say.

articles.summary: A man is dead after being injured by construction equipment in Scarborough, police say. Toronto police and paramedics responded to the area of McNicoll Avenue and Tapscott Road, near Markham Road and Steeles Avenue, just before noon on Wednesday. articles.title: 'There's no 2.0': Ford dismisses Toronto's bid for new funding agreement
articles.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he won't be signing a formal new funding agreement with the City of Toronto, even as city hall pitches for long-term help from Queen's Park. Ford, however, did signal some money could be unlocked for public safety.

articles.title: First Nations Bank gets $15M investment from Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation
articles.summary: TORONTO — First Nations Bank of Canada has announced a $15-million investment by the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation.

articles.title: 23 charged, $7.5M in drugs seized in cannabis trafficking bust: York police
articles.summary: York Regional Police say they have seized $7.5 million worth of drugs after an investigation into a criminal group allegedly involved in a wide-ranging operation of producing, trafficking and exporting illegal cannabis. articles.title: Specialty food bank that caters to Durham Region residents looking for home indoors
articles.summary: A food bank that caters to residents in Durham Region with complex health and dietary needs is looking for a new home indoors.

articles.title: Why Mississauga, Brampton residents should care about the U.S. midterms
articles.summary: With Americans heading to the polls Tuesday, CBC’s Nav Nanwa examines how the U.S. midterm results could ripple through Peel’s automotive and steel sectors.

articles.title: Arrests made in protests of Bloor Street bike lane removal intended to quell dissent, lawyers allege
articles.summary: Four people arrested last month during protests against the removal of Etobicoke bike lanes and their lawyers say Toronto police laid "heavy-handed criminal charges" against them to deter future protests — an allegation the police service refutes.

articles.title: Man dead, SIU investigating after incident at U of T Mississauga: police
articles.summary: Police say one person has been found dead and a shelter-in-place order that was issued late Monday has been lifted after officers responded to a dangerous weapons call at a University of Toronto dormitory in Mississauga.
